newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng seen testing 14,000 again.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng seen testing 14,000 again.

text.p: Hong Kong's blue-chip Hang Seng Index is expected to reach new records in the coming week after storming to all-time highs last week, but prices could consolidate briefly before tackling new peaks, analysts said.
"Overall, the market trend remains quite positive so after it ends its consolidation, it will try to test the 14,000 level," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
The Hang Seng Index closed at fresh records for three days in a row last week, ending at an all-time closing high of 13,856.40 points on Friday, up 664.90 points, or 5.04 percent, on the week.
The index rose above 14,000 points for the first time last Thursday and registered an intra-day record high of 14,004.93.
Kwong said the Hang Seng could trade between 13,600 and 14,100 points this week.

"I think the market tone is still quite upbeat and in general it might do a bit better," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities. "It is quite likely that it will test 14,000 again."

Analysts said expectations of strong earnings reports from Hong Kong's banks would continue to boost shares in the banking sector. "Usually, banks do better before their results announcements," Tsang said.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc, which reports its 1996 earnings on March 3, rose 8.9 percent last week to close at HK$183 on Friday.
"In general, 1996 was still a very good year for banks despite growing competition in the second half of the year. The buoyant property market also helped their earnings," Tsang said.
He expected Hong Kong's major banks to report earnings growth of between 18 and 20 percent for 1996.
"We also have a very bullish property market," he added. "A buoyant property market makes everyone happy."
Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities, said he expected the Hang Seng Index to drop to around 13,650 points this week before attempting to test 14,000 points again.
"I don't think the market is strong enough to break above the 14,000 level significantly," he said.
Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities, said the index could break through 14,000 if the market received positive news during the week.
But he expected a range of 13,700 to 14,000 points this coming week. "It is possible to break through before Chinese New Year. The fundamentals are still very strong."
The Chinese New Year holidays begin on February 6.
Strong investor sentiment could help the market debuts of souvenir maker Yip's Pota International Co Ltd and printing firm Cheong Ming Holdings Ltd on Monday.
But analysts said the low subscription levels for both initial public offerings (IPO) pointed to only moderate gains at the start of trade.

Yip's Pota offered 50 million shares at HK$1 each in an IPO which was 6.7 times subscribed and Cheong Ming offered 80 million shares at HK$1 per share in an IPO which was 16.9 times subscribed. ($1 = HK$7.8)
